title: One Doctrine, Two Fruits
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Central Question: Are the Fruits the Same?
subpoints: Comparing John the Baptist's demand in Luke 3 with Paul's description in 2 Corinthians 7
Identifying the shared doctrine of repentance despite different contexts
Distinguishing between internal and external angles of repentance

outline.title: John the Baptist's Fruit: External Change in Neighborly Relations
subpoints: Rejecting reliance on covenant membership or lineage (Abraham)
The urgency of judgment: the axe laid to the root
Specific, verifiable actions: generosity, honesty, and contentment
Fruit that is observable by unbelievers over time

outline.title: Paul's Fruit: Internal Response to Confronted Sin
subpoints: Godly sorrow as the root of true repentance
Seven marks of genuine repentance: diligence, clearing, indignation, fear, desire, zeal, and vindication
Immediate pursuit of change rather than delay
Holy anger directed at sin, not the messenger

summary: In this afternoon message, Pastor Tito Lyro explores the doctrine of repentance by comparing two distinct biblical passages: Luke 3:7-14 and 2 Corinthians 7:8-12. Titled "One Doctrine, Two Fruits," the sermon addresses how John the Baptist and the Apostle Paul, though operating in different contexts, both use the metaphor of fruit to describe the evidence of true repentance. The central question posed is whether the fruits demanded by John and described by Paul are identical, leading to the conclusion that while the underlying doctrine is the same, the specific manifestations differ based on the angle of observation.
